title: Retiring InfoPath: 30+ forms rebuilt in SPFx
summary: Every InfoPath form on the company’s SharePoint 2013/2016 sites — and the SharePoint Designer workflows behind them — rebuilt as SPFx React forms and Power Automate flows, ahead of Microsoft’s support deadline.
situation: The company's day-to-day processes ran on InfoPath forms in SharePoint 2013 and 2016, with SharePoint Designer workflows handling approvals and notifications. Microsoft is ending support for both.
work: Rebuilt each InfoPath form as a responsive SPFx React form.
Moved every SharePoint Designer workflow to Power Automate, keeping the same approval chains and notification rules.
Shipped in small batches so each department switched over with minimal disruption.
outcome: 30+ forms rebuilt and live in SPFx.
All their SharePoint Designer workflows replaced by Power Automate.
Programme completed.
before: Business processes ran on InfoPath forms, a product Microsoft has retired.
Approvals and notifications depended on SharePoint Designer workflows, which Microsoft is also retiring.
The forms were built for desktop browsers and did not work well on phones.
Every month on the old stack added risk: no fixes, no new features, and a hard end-of-support date.

title: Stabilising 14 SharePoint on-prem apps for a US logistics company
summary: Expense, accident-report and approval apps on an ageing SharePoint farm were creating duplicate records every day. I found the race conditions, fixed 50+ broken workflows and rebuilt the Accident Report app from scratch.
situation: WARD ran 14+ business-critical applications — expenses, accident reports, approvals — on an ageing SharePoint on-premises environment.
Forms were creating duplicate entries, the sequential ID generators kept breaking, and an unstable Node setup made every fix risky. Staff felt it every day.
work: Traced the duplicates to front-end race conditions when two people submitted at the same time, and fixed them.
Upgraded the Node versions the apps depended on.
Rebuilt the Accident Report application end-to-end with a new UI and a reliable back end.
Fixed 50+ SharePoint Designer workflows across the portfolio.
outcome: All 14+ applications stable.
Zero duplicate submissions after the fix.
New Accident Report application live in production.
before: Forms created duplicate records whenever two people submitted at the same time (a front-end race condition).
Sequential ID generators kept breaking, so records lost their reference numbers.
Unstable, outdated Node versions made every fix risky.
50+ SharePoint Designer workflows were failing across the app portfolio.
The Accident Report app was too unreliable to patch and had to be rebuilt.

title: Closing an external sharing leak in SharePoint Online
result: All unauthorised access removed within 48 hours
summary: A sharing misconfiguration had exposed internal documents to users at a partner company. I audited the tenant, revoked every unauthorised link and guest, and rebuilt the sharing policy so it couldn't happen again.
situation: An external sharing setting in SharePoint Online had been left too open. Sensitive internal documents were reachable by users at a Canadian partner organisation, and the exposure ran across several site collections.
Nobody knew exactly how far it went. The first job was to find out — quickly — and stop it.
work: Audited the whole tenant with PowerShell and the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Listed every externally shared link, guest account and anonymous access link.
Revoked access in a controlled order so business-critical sharing wasn't broken by accident.
Reset sharing policy at both tenant and site-collection level.
Added monitoring alerts and Conditional Access rules to catch drift early.
outcome: 100% of unauthorised external access removed within 48 hours.
Sharing policy tightened and enforced with Conditional Access.
Incident report delivered to stakeholders.
No recurrence since the fix.
before: Tenant-level external sharing was set far too open.
Sensitive internal documents were reachable by users at a partner organisation.
The exposure ran across several site collections, not just one.
Old sharing links, guest accounts and anonymous links had piled up with nobody reviewing them.
No alerting existed to catch over-sharing when it happened.

title: Moving 5,000 people from Google Workspace to Microsoft 365
summary: Drive, Shared Drives, Sites, Gmail and Groups — the whole Google workplace moved to Microsoft 365 inside six months, with a tracking app so everyone could see where each workload stood.
situation: A large enterprise wanted off Google Workspace entirely: Drive, Shared Drives, Google Sites, Gmail and Groups. The deadline was six months and the business couldn't stop working while it happened.
work: Google Drive and Shared Drives to SharePoint with ShareGate and Migration Manager.
Google Sites to SharePoint, classic and modern.
Gmail to Exchange Online / Outlook.
Google Groups to Microsoft 365 Groups and Teams.
Built a migration tracking app so the team could follow every workload in real time instead of chasing spreadsheets.
outcome: 5,000+ users migrated within the six-month window.
Cutover completed with zero data loss.
Replaced the client's legacy Google Sheets workflows with a governed SharePoint application after go-live.
before: The whole workplace was split across Google Drive, Shared Drives, Sites, Gmail and Groups.
Day-to-day processes ran on Google Sheets with no governance or audit trail.
A hard six-month deadline, and the business could not stop working during the move.
No single view of migration progress across workloads.

title: An internal AI assistant on Azure OpenAI and SharePoint
summary: A GenAI assistant that searches SharePoint content and handles routine requests for several departments, built with Azure OpenAI, Copilot APIs and an SPFx front end.
situation: Several departments were spending time answering the same questions and processing the same standard requests, and finding documents in SharePoint wasn't easy.
work: Designing the assistant around Azure OpenAI and Microsoft 365 Copilot APIs, with an SPFx interface inside SharePoint.
Running alongside it: a standalone Security Guard application and a Freshworks ITSM integration that creates tickets automatically.
outcome: R&D phase complete.
Proof of concept live for 2 departments.
Production rollout under way, with more departments planned.
before: Several departments spent hours answering the same questions again and again.
Standard requests were processed by hand.
Finding the right document in SharePoint was slow.

title: Internal risk, leave and resourcing apps at EY GDS
summary: SPFx React apps on SharePoint for risk workflows, leave tracking, resource allocation and onboarding — all shipped through EY's formal change-request and release process.
situation: EY GDS needed a set of internal applications — risk workflow management, leave tracking, resource allocation and employee onboarding — built to EY's security and change-management standards, with formal release schedules.
work: Designed and deployed SPFx React applications with SharePoint as the back end.
Built the internal leave and resource allocation systems.
Owned 100+ Power Automate workflows.
Handled all internal releases for the fiscal year and kept 20+ live apps moving through Change Request Management.
outcome: Full internal workflow suite in production.
100+ automations maintained.
Every release went through formal SDLC and change control, with zero compliance breaches.
swap: A new app suite, under strict change control
before: Risk workflow management, leave tracking, resource allocation and onboarding all needed proper applications.
Everything had to meet EY’s security standards.
Every change had to go through formal change-request management and scheduled releases.

title: World-clock and weather web parts for a Dubai intranet
summary: Custom SPFx web parts — a multi-timezone world clock and calendar, and a live regional weather panel — for a modern SharePoint intranet serving staff across several countries.
situation: A large food company in Dubai wanted its modern SharePoint intranet to be useful to staff spread across several countries. They needed live, local information that SharePoint doesn't provide out of the box.
work: Built custom SPFx web parts in React and TypeScript.
A world clock and calendar web part covering every office time zone.
A live weather web part with region-specific data pulled from REST APIs.
outcome: Web parts delivered and live on the intranet.
Better intranet engagement from international staff across multiple offices.
before: Staff were spread across offices in several countries and time zones.
SharePoint’s out-of-the-box web parts had no world clock, multi-zone calendar or live local weather.
The intranet needed to feel useful day to day, not just be a document store.

title: Replacing ungoverned spreadsheets with 50+ business apps
summary: After each migration wave, clients were left running core processes on complex Google Sheets and manual workflows. I rebuilt them as governed Microsoft applications with proper access control and audit trails.
before: Core business processes ran on complex Google Sheets after each migration wave.
Workflows were manual, with no approvals, notifications or audit trail.
Access to sensitive data was not governed.
The spreadsheets did not scale as usage grew.
situation: After each cloud migration wave, clients had dozens of complex Google Sheets, manual workflows and ungoverned spreadsheets. They needed proper Microsoft applications with the same functionality, but better security, scalability and audit trails.
work: Analysed each Google Sheet for its business logic.
Rebuilt each one as a governed application: SPFx React web parts, Power Apps canvas and model-driven apps, or Dataverse-backed solutions.
Added Power Automate workflows, proper access controls, and SharePoint list or Dataverse back ends.
outcome: 50+ business applications delivered across multiple clients.
Legacy Google Sheets workflows replaced with governed Microsoft solutions.
200+ Power Automate flows built to support the application portfolio.

title: An internal audit application and an ITSM workspace built from scratch
result: Audit app live, ITSM workspace operational
summary: A SharePoint audit application for capturing and tracking audit data across departments, plus a Freshworks IT service management workspace configured from scratch, with role-based access, automated routing and escalation.
swap: No structured audit or IT service desk
before: No structured way to capture and track audit data across departments.
No department-level reporting or approval trail for audit work.
No configured IT service management workspace: no role-based access, routing or escalation.
situation: The organisation needed a structured Internal Audit Application, plus a fully configured IT service management workspace in Freshworks with role-based access, automated routing and field manager workflows.
work: Built the Internal Audit Application on SharePoint with SPFx React: structured data capture, department-level reporting and Power Automate approval workflows.
Configured the Freshworks ITSM workspace from scratch: role-based access controls, field manager workflows, automated service request routing and escalation rules.
outcome: Internal Audit Application live with a full audit trail.
Freshworks ITSM workspace operational, with automated request routing, field manager workflows and structured escalation paths.
Further areas for Freshworks optimisation identified.
